subject: physics
question_text: What is Reynolds number? What is its significance?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.109). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The four-way mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: Re = ρvD/η with D the diameter of the tube, ρ the density, v the speed and η the coefficient of viscosity; it is dimensionless because all these units cancel, and it decides streamline flow below about Re = 1000, turbulent flow above about Re = 2000, with an unsteady region between.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: What the number decides
lines: The Reynolds number is a pure
flow of a fluid in a tube is
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say what the number decides before writing the formula.
steps.why: The question asks what the Reynolds number is before it asks for the formula — stating what it decides is the definition.
common_mistakes: Starting straight with the formula without saying what the number is for.
Calling it a physical quantity with a unit; it is a pure number.

recall.must_convey: That the Reynolds number is a pure number deciding whether flow is streamline or turbulent.
reject: Re equals rho v D by eta

steps.memory_tip: Reynolds number: one number, decides streamline or turbulent.

steps.label: The formula
lines: where ρ is the density, v the
speed, D the diameter of the tube
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Write the formula and name every symbol, D as the diameter.
steps.why: D is the tube's diameter, not its radius — writing the wrong symbol here changes the number by a factor of two.
common_mistakes: Writing D as the radius of the tube; D is the diameter.

recall.must_convey: That Re = ρvD/η with D the diameter of the tube, ρ the density, v the speed, η the viscosity.
accept: density times speed times diameter over viscosity

steps.memory_tip: Re = ρvD/η — D is the full diameter, not the radius.

steps.label: Why it has no unit
lines: number therefore has no unit and
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Say the units cancel, so Re has no unit and no dimensions.
steps.why: Building the number this way is what lets a dimensionless number be compared directly across different fluids and different tubes.
common_mistakes: Assigning the Reynolds number a unit such as m/s.
Saying it has dimensions but no SI unit — it has neither.

recall.must_convey: That the Reynolds number has no unit and no dimensions.
reject: formula Re equals rho v D by eta

steps.memory_tip: Every unit cancels in Re — that is why it has none of its own.

steps.label: The significance
lines: Its significance: for flow in a
tube, when Re is below about 1000
the flow is streamline; when Re is
between the two the flow is
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Give both boundary values, not just one.
steps.why: Being able to predict streamline or turbulent flow just from Re, without measuring the flow directly, is exactly why the number is useful.
common_mistakes: Quoting only one of the two boundary values.
Saying the flow is turbulent for every Re above 1000; the region up to 2000 is unsteady, not yet turbulent.

recall.must_convey: That below about 1000 the flow is streamline, above about 2000 it is turbulent, and it is unsteady in between.
reject: Re equals rho v D by eta

steps.memory_tip: Below 1000, streamline. Above 2000, turbulent. In between, unsteady.

insider_note: Two parts to this question: the definition with its formula, and the significance with both boundary values of Re.
